sentences.en: What does your new colleague look like?
She's tall and has curly hair.
What kind of person is he?

sentences.ar: هي واثقة من نفسها دون غرور.

sentences.en: He is good at explaining things.
My sister is creative and curious.
My brother is quieter than I am.
He's a little shy at first.
I admire her sense of humor.
She's reliable when things get difficult.
sentences.ar: يمكن الاعتماد عليها عندما تصبح الأمور صعبة.

sentences.en: I try not to judge people too quickly.
sentences.ar: أحاول ألّا أحكم على الناس بسرعة.

sentences.en: I enjoy talking to people from different backgrounds.
sentences.ar: أستمتع بالحديث مع أناس من خلفيات مختلفة.

sentences.en: She has a calm way of speaking.

sections.heading: Getting started
paragraphs: Dina was exploring people and descriptions. The aim was to have a clear, natural conversation in English. Dina said, “What does your new colleague look like?” A friend replied, “She's tall and has curly hair.” Dina said, “He usually wears glasses.” A friend replied, “She has a friendly smile.” They paused to remember the meaning. Dina said, “He's easy to recognize.” A friend replied, “What kind of person is he?” Dina said, “He's patient and thoughtful.” A friend replied, “She's confident without being arrogant.” They paused to remember the meaning. Dina said, “He is good at explaining things.”

sections.heading: In conversation
paragraphs: The conversation continued, and Dina practiced listening and responding with care. Dina said, “She listens carefully to others.” A friend replied, “My manager is very organized.” Dina said, “My sister is creative and curious.” A friend replied, “My brother is quieter than I am.” They paused to remember the meaning. Dina said, “We have very different personalities.” A friend replied, “He's a little shy at first.” Dina said, “She becomes talkative around friends.” A friend replied, “I admire her sense of humor.” They paused to remember the meaning. Dina said, “He always keeps his promises.”

sections.heading: Practicing details
paragraphs: Next, Dina practiced phrases that could help with common problems and decisions. Dina said, “She's reliable when things get difficult.” A friend replied, “He can be stubborn sometimes.” Dina said, “Nobody is perfect.” A friend replied, “I try not to judge people too quickly.” They paused to remember the meaning. Dina said, “First impressions can be misleading.” A friend replied, “We share the same interests.” Dina said, “I enjoy talking to people from different backgrounds.” A friend replied, “She has a calm way of speaking.” They paused to remember the meaning.

sections.heading: Putting it together
paragraphs: Before finishing, Dina reviewed more useful sentences and noticed real improvement. Dina said, “He treats everyone with respect.” A friend replied, “I appreciate honest people.” Dina said, “She's always willing to help.” A friend replied, “He pays attention to small details.” They paused to remember the meaning. Dina said, “They make a great team.” A friend replied, “We get along well despite our differences.” Dina said, “I hope to get to know them better.” A friend replied, “Everyone has a unique story.” They paused to remember the meaning.
